title: Numerical semiampleness of projective adjoints
exact_target: For a projective rational klt pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, assume $K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective and M is a nef rational Cartier divisor. If $D=K_X+B+M$ is nef, must D be numerically equivalent to some semiample rational Cartier divisor?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For a projective rational klt pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, assume $K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective and M is a nef rational Cartier divisor. If $D=K_X+B+M$ is nef, must D be numerically equivalent to some semiample rational Cartier divisor?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For a projective rational klt pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, assume $K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective and M is a nef rational Cartier divisor. If $D=K_X+B+M$ is nef, must D be numerically equivalent to some semiample rational Cartier divisor?
